newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks retreat in London as FTSE falls.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks retreat in London as FTSE falls.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks fell on profit-taking in London on Thursday after a strong performance in Asia overnight that saw the key blue chip index rise above the 12,000 level for the first time since February 1994.
By 1154 GMT, the Hang Seng London Reference Index was down 25.71 to 11,988.85.
In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng index gained 62.68 points to close at 12,022.38.
But index futures closed at a discount to the spot market, weighing Hong Kong shares in London, a London broker said.
The market fell under additional pressure as the FTSE 100 lost its grounding around midmorning.
Hong Kong shares, the broker said, "have had a good run and we're just seeing some profit-taking ahead of the U.S. employment figures."
The U.S. jobs report for September, which is expected to provide the freshest clues on inflationary pressures in the U.S., is due for release tomorrow.
The Hong Kong property sector, which the the rally recently, were hit hardest in London, he said. Bank shares, however, held firm near their closing levels in Hong Kong, he added.
